_comment: Fragment 58 — D-103: the first Sprint-boundary handover. Lane B is Active; the three gaps the handover itself opens. Merged 2026-08-24.

nodes.label: D-103 — The First Sprint-Boundary Handover
nodes.description: The build lane is selected as the one lane permitted to commit and the orchestration lane steps out. The four-state model had existed for two decisions without ever being exercised.
nodes.rationale: The orchestration lane had held the active state since the table was written, so exactly-one-active was true by inertia rather than by any act or control. A handover is two edits, and a half-applied one is the failure mode nobody had needed to think about yet.

nodes.label: Active Is Permission to Commit, Never Permission to Look
nodes.description: Three carve-outs accompany the handover. Writing in the handoff directory is always permitted; provisioning a dependency is not; reading anything always is.
nodes.rationale: Without the first carve-out the receipt check would go permanently red the moment the working lane raised anything, because no permitted act could clear it. A red that nothing can clear is the property that makes a control get ignored.

nodes.label: The Dependency Stop Is Kept, Not Carved Out
nodes.description: Build configuration belongs to the orchestration lane, which cannot commit while another lane is active, so a mid-sprint dependency request genuinely stops until the next boundary.
nodes.rationale: The rule that the orchestration lane provisions ahead exists so this is rare, and carving out an exception would remove the pressure that keeps it rare while handing a second lane write access to build configuration. The blocking entry stops that item, not the lane.

nodes.label: Check 15 — A Half-Applied Handover Fails
nodes.description: Reads the phase register by column name and fails unless exactly one lane is active, every state is one of the four, and a blocked row names what blocks it.
nodes.rationale: The surface-crossing check reads which files a change touches, not which lane may commit, so it would report a perfectly clean single-lane change made by a lane with no permission to make it. Two active rows is the silent-overwrite condition the rule files open with.

nodes.label: A Work Order Beside the Surface, Not a Condition in the Register
nodes.description: The verification condition lived in the decision register, which the build lane is explicitly not expected to read. It is restated as a work order in an orchestration-owned directory, the same arrangement the CI lane already has.
nodes.rationale: A ruling filed where its executor cannot see it has not been propagated. That was the parent finding of an earlier entry, and the condition written to answer it repeated it one pass later.

nodes.label: A Verification That Cannot Fail Is Not a Verification
nodes.description: Ten entries await independent confirmation and no rejection resolution exists yet. The interim rule is that a failed verification is raised as a new entry rather than absorbed by editing the old one.
nodes.rationale: Leaving an entry provisional after checking it destroys the evidence that it was checked, so the record has to be a separate artifact. A pass that confirms every item and rejects none is the same failure as a check that cannot fail, wearing a reviewer's hat.
